title: “The”: sun and moon letters
goal: Read al- correctly before any letter, and handle the silent alif when words join.

understand.p: Arabic's word for “the” is الْ (al-), attached to the front of a noun. When it's added, the tanwīn goes away: قَمَرٌ qamarun (a moon) → الْقَمَرُ al-qamaru (the moon).

understand.h: Moon letters: the l is heard

understand.rule: Before the 14 sun letters ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن, the ل is written but silent, and the next letter gets a shadda. Before the other 14 moon letters, the ل is pronounced.

understand.tip: Shortcut: sun letters are all made with the tip of the tongue (t, d, s, n, r…). Moon letters are made with the lips or the back of the mouth (b, m, k, q…).

understand.h: The silent alif when words join

understand.p: The alif of al- is only pronounced at the very start of speech. After another word, it's skipped and you slide straight into the l: فِي الْبَيْتِ is read fil-bayti, not fī al-bayti.

practice.why: ش is a sun letter: the l assimilates.

practice.q: Is ك a sun letter or a moon letter?
practice.why: k is made at the back of the mouth: moon.

practice.q: Is ن a sun letter or a moon letter?
practice.why: n is made with the tongue tip: sun.
